ideas.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ideas.timeframe: 6–12 months (through FY27 earnings cycle; nearest catalyst August 26 Q2 FY27 earnings)
ideas.idea: NVDA is the dominant structural AI infrastructure position. Conviction maintained at HIGH through the Stop Day 2 binary (determined July 6 US close) — the short-term tactical stop protocol does not alter the 12-month Blackwell Ultra / sovereign AI capex thesis. Half-size from July 1 ($200.09) held. OTC reference $197.16 (above $195 stop) suggests Stop Day 1 isolation probability is high going into July 6. Full-size add conditional on July 7 open (NVDA >$200 + SPX >7,460 + VIX <17 simultaneously at 9:25 AM ET). CRITICAL H200 CHINA UPDATE: Policy authorized January 16, 2026 (BIS rule, 25% tariff, case-by-case licensing) but China has NOT yet permitted imports and zero H200 revenue has been generated. The 'China reopening catalyst' is a FUTURE event — first import licenses not yet issued. When licenses are issued, this unlocks $7–10B in annualized China revenue not modeled in Street estimates. August 26 Q2 FY27 earnings ($91B guide) is the fundamental re-rating event. Nicholas Parker (MSFT field operations) joining NVIDIA as field ops head signals enterprise GTM scale-up. Vera Rubin platform progression and NVIDIA Halos for Robotics expand the total addressable market beyond data center compute.
ideas.why: Blackwell Ultra (GB300 NVL72 = 1.5x GB200 performance) is shipping. Sovereign AI capex from EU, Japan, Saudi Arabia, UAE confirmed at $100B+ combined. NVDA's CUDA software moat requires 18–24 months to replicate — AMD and Intel cannot close in FY27. Every major hyperscaler (MSFT Azure, GOOGL Cloud, AWS, META) committed multi-year NVDA GPU purchases in Q1 2026 earnings calls — not cancellable on short-term sentiment. China H200 import licenses (when issued) represent the single largest unmodeled positive catalyst for NVDA in 2026 — $7–10B annualized revenue not in current Street estimates. The stop protocol is a position management tool, not a thesis invalidation signal.
ideas.driver: China H200 import license issuance (first licenses expected Q3 2026; unlocks $7–10B annualized China revenue not in Street estimates); Blackwell Ultra GB300 GPU ramp H2 2026 (1.5x performance vs GB200; 3x compute density vs H100); sovereign AI capex ($100B+ combined); inference demand scaling faster than training as AI moves from development to deployment at scale; Q2 FY27 earnings August 26 ($91B guide); Rubin architecture roadmap 2027 extending moat; Nicholas Parker (MSFT) enterprise GTM scaling
ideas.risk: Stop Day 2 triggers July 6 (mandatory exit July 7 — short-term forced selling, not fundamental change); China H200 import licenses delayed past 2026 (removes primary re-rating catalyst); AMD MI400 achieves competitive CUDA-equivalent software ecosystem within 12 months; hyperscaler AI capex cuts H1 2027 if AI monetization disappoints; Warsh rate hold through 2028 compresses 35x forward multiple

ideas.name: Micron Technology
ideas.timeframe: 3–6 months (through Q4 FY26 earnings September 2026; structural 12–18 months through HBM4 supercycle)
ideas.idea: MU is the most compelling near-term AI semi structural buy. Conviction maintained at HIGH. The Apple/CXMT/YMTC mobile DRAM narrative is a MICRON STRUCTURAL POSITIVE: mobile DRAM share shifting to CXMT (Pentagon 1260H blacklisted) amplifies the US government AI procurement mandate for Micron's Idaho HBM4. DoD cannot use CXMT by law — every HBM4 wafer from Micron's Idaho CHIPS Act fab is DoD-compliant by jurisdiction. $50B Q4 FY26 guide (+40% above prior consensus) confirmed; HBM4 sold out through 2026. No stop protocol, no gate conditions, no ADR mechanics — cleanest structural long in the portfolio. July 6 open creates the first post-triple-holiday tactical entry at $1,150–$1,200 on any Korea-sympathetic dip.
ideas.why: The CXMT/YMTC blacklist amplification thesis is underappreciated by the Street: DoD AI procurement mandates specifically require US-manufactured memory, and CXMT's blacklist status makes Chinese DRAM non-compliant for the entire US government AI pipeline. KOSPI +5.76% + SK Hynix +10.88% recovery on July 3 KST validated the structural Korean semiconductor thesis — MU is the US proxy for that same HBM4 demand cycle. Samsung $226B AI data center commitment validates Micron's $50B Q4 guide at national-government scale. The HBM market structural oligopoly (Samsung/SK Hynix/Micron) enforces pricing discipline — no fourth entrant can reach HBM4 EUV production at commercial scale in the next 24 months. Idaho CHIPS Act cost advantage vs Korean competitors is a permanent structural feature.
ideas.driver: HBM4 ramp through H2 2026 ($50B Q4 FY26 guide confirmed); CHIPS Act Idaho fab DoD compliance advantage over CXMT/YMTC (Pentagon 1260H blacklist amplification); DoD AI procurement mandate for US-manufactured HBM; September Q4 FY26 earnings confirming HBM demand cycle duration and HBM4 ASP premium; oligopolistic HBM pricing discipline (3-player market, no 4th entrant possible in 24 months); KOSPI semiconductor recovery validating HBM cycle duration
ideas.risk: HBM demand cycle peaks H1 2027 earlier than expected as AI model efficiency gains reduce memory per compute unit; Samsung aggressive HBM4 pricing to defend NVIDIA share; Q4 FY26 guide miss at September earnings (largest single downside risk); China export controls expand to Idaho fab inputs; Micron yield issues at sub-10nm EUV node; NVDA supply diversification reduces MU HBM4 share

ideas.name: Meta Platforms
ideas.idea: META carries the highest long-term conviction of any big-tech name on a risk-adjusted basis. Conviction maintained at HIGH. The most direct AI-to-revenue conversion path in the portfolio: every AI ad targeting improvement reaches 3.3B daily active users in real-time without enterprise sales cycles, semiconductor sourcing complexity, or geopolitical trade risk. Zero exposure to Korea shock, H200 China policy, HBM4 supply chain, or BTC gates. FCF $60B+ annual makes META the most rate-resistant large-cap AI name in the Warsh hawkish hold environment. Q2 2026 earnings (late July) is the first full AI-feature quarter at scale — setup for beat and raise. Add on any July 7 post-holiday weakness.
ideas.why: 3.3B daily active users is an unassailable data and distribution moat. Llama 4 open-source flywheel builds developer ecosystem lock-in with no chip dependency. Zuckerberg AI personal assistant has genuine distribution at scale — improvements reach 3.3B users immediately. The monetization feedback loop has zero lag. META is uniquely insulated from every geopolitical and semiconductor risk identified in this framework. Every macro event in Q3 2026 (Korea shock, China H200 policy, BTC gates, NVDA stop) is zero-impact on META's revenue model — this makes META the risk-adjusted anchor of the big-tech allocation.
ideas.driver: AI ad efficiency compounding at 3.3B user scale (CPM expansion and click-through rate improvement simultaneous); Llama 4 open-source flywheel building developer ecosystem lock-in; AR/AI glasses integration (Ray-Ban Meta) approaching hardware/software platform status; Q2 2026 earnings late July = first AI-at-scale quarter; FCF $60B+ annual providing rate-resilient floor in Warsh hawkish hold environment

ideas.name: Microsoft Corporation
ideas.idea: Microsoft is the most diversified AI monetization play with the strongest rate resilience in the big-tech complex. Conviction maintained at MEDIUM. Azure AI cloud (OpenAI partnership exclusive enterprise deployment), Copilot productivity suite (400M+ 365 commercial seats at $30/month premium), GitHub Copilot (developer workflow capture). No Korea semiconductor exposure. No SPCX bond distribution mechanics. NVDA OTC $197.16 above $195 stop — Nicholas Parker joining NVIDIA from MSFT signals MSFT is a talent-exporter to AI infrastructure, not a talent destination (structural read: NVDA is becoming the enterprise field ops focal point, which is MSFT Azure cloud-constructive). Q3 BUY regime upgrade confirms the enterprise AI adoption tailwind — Copilot seat expansion is the primary revenue driver in 2026. FOMC Warsh hawkish hold through 2027 pressures growth multiples, but MSFT's $100B+ FCF and ~2% dividend yield provide a valuation floor that pure-growth AI names lack.
ideas.why: Enterprise AI adoption in 2026 is about Copilot seat conversion, not new product launches. 400M+ commercial 365 seats converting at 10–20% to Copilot Premium at $30/month = 2.5x revenue per seat vs. base tier. Azure AI workloads are sticky: switching cost is 12–24 months of enterprise IT re-integration. Goldilocks NFP + US BUY regime = enterprise IT budget cycle continues expanding through FY27. OpenAI exclusivity for enterprise Azure fine-tuning creates a 3–5 year switching friction moat. MSFT's $100B+ FCF floor means even a multiple compression from 32x to 25x forward leaves intrinsic value intact.
ideas.driver: Copilot monetization at scale (400M+ 365 commercial seats, 10–20% Copilot Premium penetration at $30/month); Azure AI revenue compounding at 35%+ YoY through FY27; GitHub Copilot Enterprise expansion; sovereign AI infrastructure licensing (EU, Middle East); $100B+ FCF floor providing rate-resilient valuation support in Warsh hawkish hold environment
ideas.risk: OpenAI explores independent cloud or direct enterprise relationships (partnership deteriorates); Google Gemini or Anthropic captures enterprise AI at lower price point; FOMC rate hold through 2028 compresses MSFT multiple from 32x to 25x forward; EU AI Act compliance burden exceeds $5B; enterprise IT spending cuts if US macro deteriorates past Goldilocks

IG floor buffer improved to ~$12 (from $6.46 July 2 AH) — Korea-contagion tail risk substantially reduced by KOSPI +5.76% on July 3. Nasdaq 100 inclusion Day 10 (July 7, ~$4.3B passive) permanently embeds SPCX in QQQ/QQQM systematic flows. The $148–$165 accumulation window may be the structural 2026 entry zone — every distribution session above $150 IG floor preserves re-entry optionality. December 9 lock-up expiry (float +4% → 9–14%) creates a supply ceiling at $185–$200 that makes the $185 re-entry gate the minimum acceptable entry.
ideas.why: Space infrastructure is at the same inflection that cloud computing crossed in 2012–2014: cost curves have collapsed (Falcon 9 250+ reflights, Starship development cost-per-orbit declining 90%+ vs prior generation) but revenue generation is in commercial innings 1–2. Starlink is profitable. SpaceX DoD backlog is $10B+. Cursor AI coding assistant crosses the $500M ARR threshold for first-earnings disclosure. The December 9 lock-up expiry creates a structural supply ceiling at $185–$200 before and after September 2 earnings — the $185 re-entry gate specifically clears you of the pre-lock-up supply risk. Korea shock has ZERO direct impact on SpaceX fundamentals.

July 9–11 (re-entry gate $185 activation post-clearance); September 2 first post-IPO earnings (Starlink ARR, Starship revenue, Cursor AI $500M+, Starshield); SpaceX equity IPO optionality (2026–2027) creating retail demand for the only liquid public SpaceX vehicle; $150 IG floor institutional bid providing structural floor; improved IG buffer (~$12) reducing Korea-contagion tail
